title: WhatsApp Business Setup Guide for Pakistani Shops and Small Businesses
desc: How to set up the free WhatsApp Business app: profile, greeting and away messages, quick replies, labels, catalog and a click-to-chat link. A step-by-step guide for Pakistan.
answer: The WhatsApp Business app is a free, separate app from WhatsApp for small businesses. Install the official version, use a business number you will keep, fill in your business profile, set a greeting and an away message, save quick replies for repeated questions, use labels to track chats, and add a catalog if you sell products. Then put a click-to-chat link on your website and pages so customers can message you in one tap. It helps you reply faster, but it does not bring customers by itself.
body: p
Last verified: 26 November 2026, against WhatsApp's own business app page and news reports listed under Sources. WhatsApp changes menus often, so a button may sit in a different place on your phone.
h2
What the WhatsApp Business app is
p

It is a separate, free app made by WhatsApp for small businesses. It looks like normal WhatsApp, with extra tools for the things a shop owner does all day: answering the same questions, keeping track of who wants what, and showing products. You install it next to your personal WhatsApp or on its own, and you use a business phone number.
p

A message is an easy first step for a customer, easier than a call or a form for many people. If your number is on your shop board, your Facebook page and your Google listing, WhatsApp can be where the first enquiry starts.
h2
Step 1: Install the real app, not a copy
p

Search for "WhatsApp Business" in the Google Play Store or the Apple App Store and check that the publisher is WhatsApp LLC. Do not install copies such as GB WhatsApp or WhatsApp Plus from random websites or APK links.
p

Those are altered versions made by other people. WhatsApp says they break its terms of service, and it has warned that accounts using them can be suspended and later lost. Your customer chats are your business records, so this is not worth the risk.
h2
Step 2: Choose the number carefully
p

Use a number that belongs to the business and that you will keep. A number the customer sees on your signboard, packaging and website should not change every time a SIM is lost or an employee leaves. Keep the SIM safe and keep the number registered in your own name or the business owner's name.
p

If you already use personal WhatsApp on that number, you will need to decide whether to move it to the business app or use a different number. If you restore a WhatsApp backup while setting up, WhatsApp says your messages, media and contacts move to the business account. Think about that first if the number also has family chats.
h2
Step 3: Fill in the business profile
p

The profile is what a customer checks before they trust you. WhatsApp lets you add a business description, email, website link, address and other details a customer might want to know. Customers can also find businesses through search.
ul
Business name: the name on your signboard. Do not add extra keywords.
Description: one or two plain sentences on what you sell and where. For example, "Home-made cakes in Gulberg, Lahore. Orders by WhatsApp, delivery across the city."
Opening hours and address: keep them the same as your Google listing.
Website link: send people to a page with your products or services, not just a home page with no contact options.
Profile photo: your logo or shop front, so people recognise it.
p
If you are setting up a Google listing as well, our guide to [Google Business Profile](/blog/google-business-profile-setup-pakistan/) explains how to keep both consistent.
h2
Step 4: Turn on the greeting and away messages
p

These are automatic messages. A greeting message goes to a customer when they first message you. An away message goes out when you are closed or busy. WhatsApp describes both as a way to respond quickly, including when you are not working.
p

Keep them short and useful. A greeting could say: "Assalam o Alaikum. Thank you for messaging [shop name]. Tell us what you need and the city, and we will reply shortly." An away message could say: "We are closed now. Our hours are 10 am to 8 pm. We will reply in the morning."
p
Do not promise a reply time you cannot keep. An honest "we reply within working hours" is better than "reply in 5 minutes" followed by silence.
h2
Step 5: Save quick replies for repeated questions
p
Quick replies are saved messages you can send with a short shortcut. Write them for the questions you answer ten times a day:
ul
Price and delivery charges.
Delivery time to your main cities.
How to pay and what happens after payment.
Your address and opening hours.
Return or exchange rules, if you offer them.
p
Read each one as a customer would. If a quick reply sounds cold or copied, edit it. Add the customer's name when you send it. One customer should not feel like one more copy of the same message.
h2
Step 6: Use labels to keep track of chats
p
Labels let you sort chats and contacts so you can follow up properly. WhatsApp also notes that labels help separate work chats from personal ones. A simple set is enough:
ul
New enquiry
Waiting for payment
Order confirmed
Delivered
Follow up later
p
The point is not to look organised. It is to stop missing the customer who asked for a price three days ago and never got a second message.
h2
Step 7: Add a catalog if you sell products
p

A catalog lets customers browse, choose and share your products or services inside WhatsApp. Add clear photos, a short name, a price and a description for each item. Keep prices current. An old price in the catalog causes arguments later.
p
If you sell a few high-value services instead, such as AC repair or tuition, a catalog may be less useful. A clear profile description and a quick reply listing your services may do more.
h2
Step 8: Put a click-to-chat link on your website, page and ads
p

A WhatsApp link opens a chat with your business when someone taps it. The usual format is wa.me followed by your full number with the country code and no plus sign, spaces or leading zero. For a Pakistani mobile number 03XX-XXXXXXX, you write 92 and then the number without the 0. Open the link on your own phone before you publish it.
p

You can add a pre-filled message to the link, such as "Hello, I would like to ask about your services." That tells you where the customer came from and saves them typing. The WhatsApp buttons on this site work the same way.
p

WhatsApp also lists ads that click to WhatsApp as a way to reach new customers and start conversations. If you run [Meta Ads](/services/meta-ads-management/), a message-focused campaign can send people straight to your chat. Set up [conversion tracking](/services/conversion-tracking/) as well, so you know which ads bring real conversations and not only clicks.
h2
What the app cannot do for you
ul
It does not bring customers by itself. People need to find your number first, through your website, Google listing, social pages, packaging or ads.
It does not make a slow business fast. If nobody replies for two days, the best profile will not help.
It is not built for large teams answering from many computers. That is a different WhatsApp product, with different costs and set-up.
It does not guarantee sales. It only makes it easier for a customer to ask.
h2
Common mistakes
ul
Using GB WhatsApp or another unofficial copy.
Using a personal number that changes often.
No greeting message, so new customers wait without knowing whether anyone is there.
Quick replies that sound like a robot wrote them.
An outdated catalog with old prices.
Sending bulk messages to people who never asked to hear from you. It annoys customers, and it can lead to your number being reported.
A number printed on your board that is switched off most of the day.
h2
A simple first week
ol
Day 1: install the official app and set up the profile.
Day 2: write the greeting and away message.
Day 3: save five quick replies.
Day 4: create labels and start using them on every new chat.
Day 5: add your best ten products to the catalog, if you sell products.
Day 6: create your WhatsApp link, test it and put it on your website and social pages.
Day 7: review the week. Which questions came up most? Update your quick replies.
p

If you would like help connecting WhatsApp, your website and your ads into one clear path from first click to first message, our [free marketing audit](/free-marketing-audit/) is a simple place to start, and [how it works](/how-it-works/) explains each step. For a related read, see [Lead Generation for Service Businesses in Pakistan](/blog/lead-generation-for-service-businesses-pakistan/).

faq: Is the WhatsApp Business app free?
Yes. WhatsApp says the app is free to download. Costs only come in if you pay for ads or use other WhatsApp business products.
Can I use WhatsApp Business and personal WhatsApp on one phone?
Many people do, with a different number for each app. Check WhatsApp's current help pages for the exact rules on your phone, because they can change.
Is GB WhatsApp Business safe to use?

No. GB WhatsApp and similar apps are altered copies made by third parties. WhatsApp says they violate its terms and has warned that accounts using them can be suspended. Use only the official app from the Play Store or App Store.
What should I write in my WhatsApp Business description?
Say what you sell, where you work and how people can order, in one or two plain sentences. Skip long slogans and keyword lists.
Does WhatsApp Business get me more customers?
Not on its own. It helps you answer faster and stay organised once someone messages you. You still need people to find your number, through your website, Google listing, social media or ads.
How do I make a WhatsApp link for my website?

Use wa.me followed by your number with the country code, without the plus sign, spaces or leading zero. For a Pakistani number that starts 03, replace the 0 with 92. Test the link on your own phone before publishing it.
